title: LEFT JOIN
description: Learn how to use the LEFT JOIN clause to return all rows from the left table and matching rows from the right table.

data.alt: SQL Server LEFT JOIN - move condition to ON clause
SQL Server Left Join and WHERE clause
SQL Server LEFT JOIN - join three tables
SQL Server Left Join find unmatching rows

data.text: The LEFT JOIN is a clause of the SELECT statement that allows you to query data from multiple tables. The LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and the matching rows from the right table. If no matching rows are found in the right table, NULL values are used.

data.title: LEFT JOIN Syntax
data.content: Return all rows from T1 and matching rows from T2.
data.code:
SELECT
    select_list
FROM
    T1
LEFT JOIN T2 ON join_predicate;

data.text: In this syntax, T1 is the left table and T2 is the right table. For each row from T1, the query compares it with all rows from T2. If a pair of rows causes the join predicate to evaluate to TRUE, the column values are combined into a new row and included in the result set. If a row from the left table has no matching row from the right table, the column values from the right table are set to NULL.
In short, the LEFT JOIN clause returns all rows from the left table (T1) and matching rows or NULL values from the right table (T2).
LEFT JOIN Example with Two Tables

data.title: Products and Order Items
data.content: Each sales order item includes one product linked by product_id.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    order_id
FROM
    production.products p
LEFT JOIN sales.order_items o ON o.product_id = p.product_id
ORDER BY
    order_id;

data.text: A list of NULL values in the order_id column indicates that the corresponding products have not been sold to any customer yet.
It is possible to use the WHERE clause to limit the result set. The following query returns the products that do not appear in any sales order.

data.title: Find Products with No Sales
data.content: Use WHERE order_id IS NULL to find unmatched products.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    order_id
FROM
    production.products p
LEFT JOIN sales.order_items o ON o.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE order_id IS NULL

data.title: Joining Three Tables with LEFT JOIN
data.code:
SELECT
    p.product_name,
    o.order_id,
    i.item_id,
    o.order_date
FROM
    production.products p
    LEFT JOIN sales.order_items i ON i.product_id = p.product_id
    LEFT JOIN sales.orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
ORDER BY
    order_id;

data.text: Conditions in ON vs. WHERE Clause
The following query finds the products that belong to order id 100.

data.title: Filter with WHERE Clause
data.content: WHERE order_id = 100 filters the final result set.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    order_id
FROM
    production.products p
LEFT JOIN sales.order_items o
    ON o.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE order_id = 100
ORDER BY
    order_id;

data.text: Let's move the condition order_id = 100 to the ON clause instead.

data.title: Condition in ON Clause
data.content: Putting condition in ON keeps all products; only order_id=100 has data.
data.code:
SELECT
    p.product_id,
    product_name,
    order_id
FROM
    production.products p
    LEFT JOIN sales.order_items o
        ON o.product_id = p.product_id AND
            o.order_id = 100
ORDER BY
    order_id DESC;

data.text: The query returned all products, but only the order with id 100 has associated product information. This is because the WHERE clause filters the result set after the join, while the ON clause filters during the join.

data.title: ON vs WHERE
data.text: For INNER JOIN, conditions in the ON clause are functionally equivalent to those in the WHERE clause. For LEFT JOIN, they behave differently: ON filters before the join, WHERE filters after.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matching rows from the right table.
If no match is found in the right table, NULL values are returned.
Use WHERE IS NULL to find rows in the left table with no match in the right table.
Conditions in the ON clause filter during the join; conditions in WHERE filter after the join.
LEFT JOIN is also known as LEFT OUTER JOIN (OUTER is optional).
